research_question: Which theorem-level results most directly improve ZenoDEX deterministic parsing, immutable state, parallel execution, atomic commitment, market clearing, and formal assurance?

tiers.S: required for the normative functional-core profile
tiers.B: useful supporting architecture or bounded experiment

theorems.source: Krishnaswami and Yallop, A Typed, Algebraic Approach to Parsing, DOI:10.1145/3314221.3314625
theorems.statement: A well-typed predictive context-free expression can be parsed unambiguously with one-token lookahead, no backtracking, and linear-time behavior.
theorems.zenodex_use: Generate authority parsers whose choices are statically disjoint and whose output is a protocol command type rather than an untyped object tree.
theorems.proof_obligation: full consumption, bounded resources, stable typed errors, no duplicate keys or floats, and equivalence to a reference grammar

theorems.source: Yallop, Xie, and Krishnaswami, flap, arXiv:2304.05276
theorems.statement: Normalization of context-free expressions to a deterministic Greibach-style normal form preserves semantics and enables deterministic one-lookahead parsing.
theorems.zenodex_use: Compile a declarative protocol grammar into a small deterministic parser while retaining a certificate linking generated code to the source grammar.
theorems.proof_obligation: normalization certificate, source/generated hashes, and differential parser vectors

theorems.statement: If decoding the output of an encoder returns exactly the original typed value with no remaining input, the encoder is injective; exact accepted re-encoding gives one accepted byte spelling per value.
theorems.zenodex_use: Exclude alternate JSON, hexadecimal, integer, receipt, and signature preimages for the same semantic authority.
theorems.proof_obligation: byte-exact decoding, canonical re-encoding, duplicate-key rejection, and cross-language vectors

theorems.source: Clarke, Potter, and Noble, Ownership Types for Flexible Alias Protection, DOI:10.1145/286936.286947
theorems.statement: A sound ownership discipline restricts access paths so declared aliasing properties of well-typed object graphs remain invariant.
theorems.zenodex_use: Make committed state own every transitive child and reject retained builders and behavior-bearing subclasses at the authority boundary.
theorems.proof_obligation: constructor-alias attacks, exact protocol-type admission, transitive ownership, and root stability after external mutation

theorems.source: Birka and Ernst, A Practical Type System and Language for Reference Immutability, DOI:10.1145/1028976.1028980
theorems.statement: An immutable reference cannot be used to modify the abstract state transitively reachable through that reference.
theorems.zenodex_use: Treat committed snapshots, accepted effects, receipts, command payloads, and proof inputs as transitively immutable authority values.
theorems.proof_obligation: no public or base-class mutator bypass, no reinitializer bypass, immutable nested collections, and copy stability

theorems.source: DeLine and Fahndrich, Typestates for Objects, DOI:10.1007/978-3-540-24851-4_21
theorems.statement: A typestate discipline makes operation availability depend on protocol state and excludes illegal state transitions.
theorems.zenodex_use: Represent Parsed, Authenticated, Authorized, Evaluated, Committed, Finalized, and Settled as distinct typed phases with exhaustive transitions.
theorems.proof_obligation: complete transition table, constructor invariants, illegal-transition tests, and versioned migration relations

theorems.source: Lucassen and Gifford, Polymorphic Effect Systems, DOI:10.1145/73560.73564
theorems.statement: The statically computed effect and region description conservatively contains the actual effects of evaluation.
theorems.zenodex_use: Require each parallelizable command to expose a sound ReadSet, WriteSet, ContextSet, effect kind, and algorithm version before scheduling.
theorems.proof_obligation: read/write footprint soundness and rejection of hidden I/O, clocks, mutable caches, and dynamic undeclared reads

theorems.source: Kahn, The Semantics of a Simple Language for Parallel Programming, IFIP 1974
theorems.statement: Networks of deterministic continuous processes over monotone streams have a unique least-fixed-point denotation independent of fair interleaving.
theorems.zenodex_use: Use immutable inputs and deterministic channels or plans so worker timing and shared-memory races cannot influence consensus outputs.
theorems.proof_obligation: pure workers, fixed input snapshot, deterministic channel or patch order, termination or fairness, and no timing observations

theorems.statement: Patches with disjoint write domains commute, and every permutation of the same independent task list yields the same post-state.
theorems.zenodex_use: Parallelize only after a sound conflict graph proves independence, then compare the canonical merge with normative sequential execution.
theorems.proof_obligation: complete patches, read/write independence, common pre-state/context hash, canonical errors, and parallel-versus-sequential differential tests

theorems.statement: Each completed concurrent operation appears to take effect atomically at one point between invocation and response while respecting its sequential specification.
theorems.zenodex_use: Commit state, effects, receipt, nonce updates, roots, and outbox as one expected-root operation; a mismatch publishes nothing.
theorems.proof_obligation: linearization point, atomic storage transaction, retry idempotence, crash consistency, and no partial external effects

theorems.source: Bellare, Canetti, and Krawczyk, Keying Hash Functions for Message Authentication, DOI:10.1007/3-540-68697-5_1
theorems.statement: Security of composed keyed-hash invocations depends on structurally separated roles; ZenoDEX applies this as explicit prefix-free domains for every authority hash.
theorems.zenodex_use: Separate state roots, commands, receipts, proofs, signatures, contexts, chains, algorithms, and versions with length-delimited domains.
theorems.proof_obligation: domain registry, prefix-free framing, cross-surface collision tests, and algorithm/version binding

theorems.source: Tas, Tse, Yang, and Zindros, Light Clients for Lazy Blockchains, arXiv:2203.15968v3
theorems.statement: A bisection game over a Merkle-committed execution ledger achieves logarithmic interaction and communication with succinctness, completeness, and soundness under the paper's assumptions.
theorems.zenodex_use: Commit deterministic transition traces so a challenger can isolate the first divergent step without replaying complete history.
theorems.proof_obligation: canonical leaf encoding, transition index binding, first-divergence protocol, and explicit data-availability assumptions

theorems.source: Schlegel, Kwasnicki, and Mamageishvili, Axioms for Constant Function Market Makers, arXiv:2210.00048v4
theorems.statement: Within the paper's framework, independence plus scale invariance characterizes a generalized constant-product class, while independence plus translation invariance characterizes LMSR.
theorems.zenodex_use: Select and version curves by declared axiom profiles, then prove the integer runtime refines the profile rather than validating formulas in isolation.
theorems.proof_obligation: axiom manifest, zero-liquidity and boundary semantics, fee-adjusted invariant, and integer-runtime refinement

theorems.source: Bichuch and Feinstein, Axioms for Automated Market Makers, arXiv:2210.01227v4
theorems.statement: The paper constructs a fee structure designed so splitting one economic transaction does not alter the aggregate fee outcome.
theorems.zenodex_use: Require fee debit, fee ownership, and explicit residue to be invariant under admissible command fragmentation and batch regrouping.
theorems.proof_obligation: split/merge metamorphic tests, dust conservation, no same-transaction stake capture, and authenticated claim reachability

theorems.statement: A strict admissible supply function has a zero by Brouwer; for the paper's order-plus-AMM construction this yields a price with nonnegative token surplus and price-optimal AMM swaps.
theorems.zenodex_use: Use existence as an abstract uniform-price specification, but accept execution only through a deterministic integer approximation certificate and canonical tie-break rule.
theorems.proof_obligation: strictness or boundary certificate, fixed-point residual, integer conservation, canonical price normalization, and winner certificate

theorems.statement: Supply components supported on separated token subsets can be solved as separated equilibrium conditions under the proposition's support assumptions.
theorems.zenodex_use: Partition the token graph into certified independent components, solve them in parallel, and join only through a fixed numeraire and canonical normalization.
theorems.proof_obligation: support-graph certificate, no cross-component order or pool, shared-numeraire semantics, and component-join proof

theorems.source: Pennanen, Efficient allocations in double auction markets, arXiv:2001.02071v2
theorems.statement: In the paper's divisible-asset nonstrategic model, zero trade coincides with the Pareto frontier and repeated double auctions converge to individually rational Pareto allocations.
theorems.zenodex_use: Use as a simulation benchmark for long-run batch-market dynamics, not as a production guarantee under strategic blockchain behavior.
theorems.proof_obligation: assumption-gap analysis, strategic counterexamples, and finite-integer experiments

theorems.source: Dolev et al., Self-Stabilizing Byzantine Fault-Tolerant Repeated Consensus, arXiv:2506.12900v1
theorems.statement: The construction is intended to recover repeated Byzantine agreement from arbitrary transiently corrupted states under its stated fault and timing assumptions.
theorems.zenodex_use: Design explicit recovery epochs for Oracle, validator, and registry state rather than assuming every persisted state begins valid.
theorems.proof_obligation: fault model, convergence bound, recovery state machine, and prohibition on value movement before recovery

ideas.design: RawBytes -> CanonicalBytes -> ParsedCommand -> AuthenticatedCommand -> AuthorizedCommand -> EvaluatedCandidate -> CommittedReceipt
Every command derives exact ReadSet, WriteSet, ContextSet, EffectKind, AlgorithmVersion, and authority domains before scheduling.
Canonical command order -> sound conflict graph -> deterministic components -> pure workers -> fixed reduction tree -> canonical errors/effects.
Candidate = {next_state, effects, receipt, nonce_updates, outbox, roots}; expected-root mismatch returns no candidate.
Merkle-commit pre-root, command, context, post-root, effects, and receipt for each step; dispute by first-divergence bisection.
An untrusted optimizer proposes price/allocation; the core checks coverage, conservation, limits, residual bounds, and canonical tie-breaking.
Evaluate Sedna-style coded private dissemination outside consensus semantics; decode first, then parse canonical bytes normally.
Record theorem query, source, formal candidate, checker version, exact SHA, outcome, and unresolved obligations in an append-only evidence ledger.
Use CRDTs only for telemetry, peer discovery, caches, and rebuildable indexes; never for authoritative economic state.
Sandbox optimizers and proof generators; accept only typed bounded candidates checked by the functional core.
Use hash-consing for immutable DAG sharing with collision-safe equality; never let pointer identity or a hash alone define consensus equality.

citation_corrections.replacement: Electricity-market data-center load shifting; use revenue adequacy and cost recovery only as mechanism-design checks.
Useful for approximate off-chain computation, but normative ZenoDEX arithmetic must remain deterministic and integer-exact.

non_claims: TheoremSearch semantic similarity is not proof relevance or formal correctness.
A paper theorem is not applicable outside its stated assumptions without a refinement proof.
The Lean files prove abstract connective lemmas, not complete runtime correctness.
Parallel execution is unsafe until read/write/context footprints are proved sound.
Equilibrium existence does not supply a canonical terminating integer algorithm.
This ledger does not claim the complete ZenoDEX functional core is verified.
